Definition: to walk (literally or figuratively); causatively, to carry (in various senses)
BiblicalUsage: Yâlak is the word for going and walking, the ordinary motion of life turned into the language of obedience. Moses tells Israel to walk in all the ways the LORD has commanded, that it may be well with them, and Micah sums up the whole law as walking humbly with God. The word also covers the everyday going of tribes seeking pasture and a king going up to the high place at Gibeon, so that no step is too small for God to notice.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Christian life is a walk, not a single leap, and God measures it step by step. My position is that doing justly and loving mercy are not ideas but directions to walk in, every day. And I hold that the God who asks me to walk humbly with Him has already walked the road ahead of me.
